RefinedC.model: Caesium, i32; source-level refined ownership types

AutoCorres2.model: Default ARM C model: 32-bit pointers and int; host is x86_64

limitations: Function-level correctness under displayed preconditions; no whole-program linking, executable compiler theorem, or end-to-end binary verification was instantiated.

VST semax_body and RefinedC typed_function establish safety and functional partial correctness. Separate termination proofs were not supplied for these tools. AutoCorres2 runs_to proves total correctness; WP includes termination obligations.

VST and RefinedC array contracts own initialized arrays; WP permits read-only initialized arrays. These are different admissible memory states, including potentially different empty-array pointer domains.

P5 VST and RefinedC specify reversal of the value sequence. AutoCorres2 and the unfinished WP contract additionally preserve node identities and values. Frame specifications are not identical across tools.

AutoCorres2 P1/P3 omit limits.h, used only by ACSL in the shared source. RefinedC adds attributes, refinedc.h and a typedef for node pointers. Executable function bodies are unchanged apart from whitespace.
This is a small cold-local-build case study with prebuilt libraries and warm OS caches, not a controlled general performance ranking. RSS is a per-process high-water mark, not aggregate memory.
WP P5 stays open. No interactive Rocq discharge or certificate is claimed; no VST-A experiment was performed.
